Sports.title: Doyle: Opera Ballo the main danger to Bow Echo at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Our ambassador gives her verdict on a stellar renewal of the Sussex Stakes on Day Two of the Glorious Goodwood Festival and provides her thoughts on the rest of the card.

Hard to oppose impeccable Echo in Sussex

It's difficult to make a cast-iron case against Bow Echo as he puts his unbeaten record on the line in the Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (4.10) at the Qatar Goodwood Festival on Wednesday.

George Boughey's colt was a brilliant winner of the Guineas before following up in the St James' Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot last month and has been delighting connections in his homework since.

He takes on the older horses for the first time but a handy draw in stall four as well as that eight-pound weight-for-age allowance strengthens his case to become the fifth three-year-old winner of this Group One in the last decade.

Front running Ballo could be hard to peg back

If there's one rival who could spoil the party in the Sussex Stakes it's Godolphin's Opera Ballo who ran a game race in the Queen Anne and could prove hard to peg back on a track that is better suited to front runners like him.

Charlie Appleby's colt has been building a serious profile with wins in the Group One Jebel Hatta in Dubai and a smooth success over Field Of Gold and subsequent Summer Mile winner Zeus Olympios at Sandown.

Aidan O'Brien's admirable Gstaad, who was second to Bow Echo at the Royal Meeting, is such a street fighter but lacks the turn of foot that Bow Echo possesses at that will probably be his undoing on the Downs.

Hannon filly sets standard in Molecomb

Richard Hannon and Sean Levey hold some strong chances at Goodwood this week but none more appealing than Pershaada in the Group Three Veuve Clicquot Molecomb Stakes (3.35) on Wednesday.

This daughter of Persian Force is already a course and distance winner, landing a novice in May before running a big race in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot. She was little more than two lengths behind Victorious that day, finishing second in her group, and that form entitles her to plenty of respect in this field.

I'd love to see Rebecca Menzies win a big race like this with her unbeaten Adonius who has been kept fresh since extending his unbeaten record in the Lily Agnes at Chester and has speed to burn. It would also be nice to see Archie Watson's Flight Signal get back to the promise he showed on debut after struggling in the Norfolk Stakes.

Fabulous Flora the one to beat in Oak Tree

Flora Of Bermuda put her Royal Ascot disappointment firmly behind her in the Group Three Summer Stakes at York this month and can follow up in the Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes (3.00) at Goodwood.

Andrew Balding's course winner can take the step up to seven-furlong in her stride with a good low draw in her favour in this Group Three and can confirm this season's Newmarket form with market rival Sayidah Dariyan. She wasn't beaten far in the Group One Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot but whether she will see out seven-furlongs as well as Flora Of Bermuda is open to question.

Simon and Ed Crisford's Zanthos does have top class form at this distance having won the Group Two Rockfel Stakes at Newmarket last year but she needs to bounce back from her flop in the Commonwealth Cup with a tongue tie on for the first time.

Longer trip looks ideal for Infraad

I'm hoping my husband Tom (Marquand) can make a winning start on Wednesday in the Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap (1.50) when he partners William Haggas's smart Ghaiyyath colt Infraad.

A Pontefract novice winner, he looks ready for this step up to a mile and a half after making a promising handicap debut against more seasoned opposition at Chester a few weeks ago.

The handicapper has left him on the same mark of 90 which can give him the edge over a competitive field including Harry Eustace's Nottingham scorer Bay Royale - a taking son of New Bay who may just find more in a first-time tongue tie.

Moore booking catches my eye in finale

The closing HKJC World Pool Handicap (5.40) is wide open but the booking of Ryan Moore for Crimson Spirit can prove decisive.

Dan and Claire Kubler's five-year-old - a good second at Newmarket last time - doesn't have the best draw in stall 10 but won a big field handicap over course and distance back in May and remains fairly treated off his higher rating.

Likely favourite Bobby Bennu represents top trainer Roger Varain but hasn't won on turf for a long time and has produced his best recent form on an artificial surface. A three-pound rise makes this a tougher task so I'm happy to seek out some value with Crimson Spirit.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Why has Hamilton received so many penalties and what have they cost him?
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has received four penalties from the stewards in the last three Formula 1 race weekends - an unusually high number for any driver over such a short period.

After his latest penalty in Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix for speeding in the pit lane, Hamilton stated on the radio that the stewards are "handing out penalties like crazy".

The result was that Hamilton lost further crucial points in the title race, and he now trails Kimi Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, so have the penalties been justified?

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

British Grand Prix - false start

Finishing Position: Third

Points lost: Likely none

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New angles of Lewis Hamilton's false start at British GP

Hamilton was handed a five-second time penalty for jumping the start at the British Grand Prix when he was deemed to be creeping forward before the lights went out.

He went on to finish third, perhaps fortunately after knocking down his pit mechanic at a late pit stop, so the penalty likely did not impact his result. Hamilton considered the penalty harsh.

"We talked in the drivers' briefing the fact that they're inconsistent with this stuff. Drivers in the past have moved and not been penalised," he said.

"We discussed that, as long as you're not moving when the last lights are on, you shouldn't be penalised. I wasn't out of my box. And they agreed. So they're looking into that for the future."

Belgian Grand Prix - causing a collision

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to six

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

Hamilton was given a five-second time penalty for being "wholly at fault" for colliding with George Russell on the opening lap of the British Grand Prix at Turn 5.

On the inside line, Hamilton understeered into Russell and was "unable to maintain sufficient separation" which led to the contact and Russell spinning into the gravel and out of the race.

But, Russell himself said the contact was a "racing incident" even though he came off worse.

Hamilton said: "Even the driver I collided with said that it was just a racing incident. I think that one was not needed. But that cost me a lot of points."

Hamilton benefited from pitting and serving his penalty under a Virtual Safety Car, but without the penalty he would almost certainly have been on the podium rather than finishing fourth.

He may even have had a fighting chance of victory given his team-mate Charles Leclerc was only overtaken by race-winner Antonelli with 10 laps to go. A battle with Leclerc was definitely on the cards for second.

Hungarian Grand Prix Qualifying - impeding

Starting Position: Fifth

Impact: Potential to lead race and fight for win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's was given a grid penalty for blocking Oscar Piastri in qualifying in Hungary

Hamilton was hit with a three-grid place penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri during the final part of Qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

After completing his final Q3 run, where he did not improve, Hamilton was not told Piastri was starting his flying lap, so effectively blocked the McLaren driver through Turn 1.

"That was really just unfortunate. I take responsibility for ultimately being on track. I should have looked in my mirrors," said Hamilton.

"But I thought everyone would have been at the end of the first lap. The information I got was right at the end. A communication error."

Hamilton was not happy that Ferrari sent himself and Leclerc out first for the last Q3 runs, which partly led to the impeding incident with Piastri.

He had qualified second and, with brand-new soft tyres, would have had a golden chance to take the lead on the first lap and potentially win the race. Instead, he started fifth and was penalised again in the Grand Prix.

Hungarian Grand Prix - speeding in the pit lane

Finishing Position: Fourth

Points lost: Up to three

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson analyses Lewis Hamilton's speeding in the pit lane that handed him a five-second time penalty

The final race before the summer break was not well executed by Ferrari and Hamilton, who endured a difficult time after being overtaken by Max Verstappen after the first round of pit stops.

But Hamilton was still potentially on course for second until a Virtual Safety Car with 13 laps to go led Ferrari to pit for new fresh tyres.

In the pit lane, Hamilton exceeded the 80kph speed limit by 0.1kph as he was eager to beat Antonelli on the merge between pit exit and track.

It was a driver mistake but Hamilton thought, with hindsight, he should not have pitted and would have been third without the stop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

"The call came literally just before the pit lane entry and I didn't have time to debate and you've got to trust the decision that has been taken," he told Sky Sports F1.

"In hindsight, my tyres were totally fine. I was probably going to lose out to Max but I think I could have kept third at least. Then just opened up the door to obviously the penalty that I got in the end."

Hamilton: I can't give stewards any reason to penalise me

Apart from the Belgium collision with Russell, all of Hamilton's penalties are hard, or impossible, to argue against. He has probably only lost six points from the in-race penalties but the impeding in Qualifying at the Hungaroring was the most detrimental.

Ferrari had great pace in Budapest and track position is king, so a good start on softs from the front row of the grid likely would have seen Hamilton in the lead.

His raw speed has been very strong recently, too, so victory was possible on Sunday and he would have been less than 40 points behind Antonelli.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton responds to his speeding penalty from Budapest

Ferrari and Hamilton must cut out these unforced errors if they want that record-breaking eighth world drivers' title.

"I'll work hard to try and come back. There's still a lot of positives to take. I'm going to try and make sure I don't give them any reason to penalise me," said Hamilton.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr to stay at Real Madrid - what next for Arsenal?
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior will be staying at Real Madrid beyond this summer, Sky Sports News has been told.

The Spanish club have no intention of selling him and are confident he will agree a new contract.

This is despite the interest of Arsenal, who are monitoring his situation closely with a year remaining on his current deal.

On Monday, Sky Sports News broke the news that further talks over his future between Real and his representatives will take place this week. That is with the intention of making progress on a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu.

New manager Jose Mourinho is understood to value Vinicius highly and wants him to remain one of his top Galacticos.

What does Vinicius' future mean for Arsenal, Barcola & Diomande?

"Real Madrid are in a bit of a sticky situation because Vinicius Jr has only got one more year left on his contract. In six months from now, he could sign a pre-contract agreement with anyone outside of Spain. Then he could join any club for no money at all next summer.

“If you think about the valuation of the player, we think he is about £137m. That’s a large amount of money to forgo. However, they are confident he will sign that new deal.

“[The Diomande deal is] unaffected. I don’t think this has anything to do with Vinicius Jr at all. I suppose they may have used it to put pressure on Vinicius. He [Diomande] plays on both sides. There’s a situation where Yan Diomande can play on the right, Vinicius Jr signs his new contract and plays in his preferred position on the left, and Kylian Mbappe through the centre.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande says he is fully focused on the World Cup despite transfer speculation, but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger.

“As far as Diomande is concerned. He is continuing to train with RB Leipzig while talks with Real Madrid continue. Our colleagues from Sky in Germany are saying that the training is not that strenuous because they want to protect him. There is a feeling this deal is pretty close.

“There is a gap in valuation, but not so big that it’s insurmountable. It seems as if it is a one horse race because Paris Saint-Germain have publicly pulled out.

“Arsenal will continue to keep an eye on Vinicius Jr’s situation still. He hasn’t signed that new contract yet. As it stands, he has a year left on his contract. That’s why they are exploring the conditions of a possible deal.

“How Andrea Berta does his business at Arsenal is very clear. It’s not about one target and then the risk of that target not coming. They try to get their ducks in a row with three or four deals. Get as far down the line as they can with as many targets as possible, and then decide which player they are going to go for.

“One of those players is Bradley Barcola. He’s intimated to PSG that he’s not going to sign a new contract. That’s primarily because in the biggest games last season, he was on the bench. He doesn’t want to go through that again. It looks like he could become available for a transfer. Liverpool are interested as well and we think PSG will initially value him at £145m.”

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas:

The situation regarding Vinicius Junior has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest and further talks to come.

But there is no strong public evidence yet that Vinicius wants to leave Real Madrid for any reason, sporting or otherwise; no quotes, no interviews, no suggestive social media posts.

Real Madrid and - most importantly - new manager Jose Mourinho want him to stay and agree new terms.

Club president Florentino Perez is personally involved and has publicly expressed a desire for Vinicius to stay long term. Reports in Spain have long claimed that both parties have indicated a preference for him to remain at the club. Real Madrid do not want him to run down the deal into a free agent situation either.

Vinicius is more than just an outstanding left winger. He is a global superstar - and a Galactico in every sense. In that way he embodies everything about Real Madrid and fits right in.

Can the same be said about Arsenal? Signing such an icon has not been part of Mikel Arteta's Arsenal project so far, however exciting it might be to go in that direction.

Sports.title: Fifa accused of ‘selling the soul of football’ over $20bn World Cup commercial rights sale plan
Sports.content:
Fifa has announced plans to sell the commercial rights to its tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors in a controversial move that triggered an immediate backlash from Uefa and leading European clubs.

Uefa released a strongly-worded statement accusing Fifa of “attempting to sell the soul of football” and is believed to be considering its legal position, while sources at numerous elite clubs were highly critical of the proposal in private.

Fifa has confirmed it is working with US bank JP Morgan on setting up a new entity – to be called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) – that would raise hundreds of millions of dollars by selling a significant stake in the commercial rights of the men’s and women’s World Cups, and the Club World Cup to investors, with promises of an increase in distribution of “over $10bn” then being redistributed back to Fifa’s 211 member associations. Thrive Capital, an investment company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, is leading the search for investors.

The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, said the plan would see “the commercial side of the game [operating] as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world”. The plans are subject to approval by a “majority” of member associations, but Fifa declined to comment when asked when a vote will take place.

Numerous sources with knowledge of Fifa’s proposals said it is valuing the new commercial venture at around $20bn, with Infantino looking to cash in on football’s growing global popularity following this summer’s World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico. The Guardian revealed this month that Fifa’s revenues for the tournament would exceed $15bn, a significant increase on the projected figure of $13bn, with such growth appearing to embolden Infantino to seek further riches.

The revelation of the plans provoked an immediate backlash from Uefa, with the European governing body accusing Fifa of attempting to sell the soul of football. Relations between the two most powerful organisations in the sport are at an all-time low, with Uefa claiming Fifa undermined the integrity of the World Cup this month when it intervened to overturn the USA striker Falorin Balogun’s red card after President Trump had personally called on Infantino to do so.

“This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,” Uefa said of the FFE plan. “Uefa takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino is looking to cash in on football’s growing global popularity following this summer’s World Cup. Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not Fifa’s to sell.”

Infantino had succeeded in keeping Fifa’s plans under wraps until reports of the proposal first emerged in the Times and Financial Times. Fifa Council members are understood to have been surprised by the announcement having been sidelined from the decision-making process.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It is the second occasion that Infantino has attempted to attract private capital to fund Fifa. In 2018, he agreed a deal in principle with Japanese bank SoftBank to provide $25bn in funding for an expanded Club World Cup and global Nations League, but failed to get sufficient support, largely due to opposition from Europe. Uefa and the clubs are again united against Fifa’s plans, but Infantino may have sufficient backing from elsewhere to be able to disregard them.

In its statement, Fifa said the new enterprise would enable it to increase the funding provided to each of the associations from $8m to $20m each year, a huge sum for the majority of their 211 members. Fifa also insisted it would retain responsibility for football’s governance and the international match calendar, but in reality inviting private investment in their commercial rights would subject the decision makers to significant external pressures. External investors could ultimately be given significant influence over decisions that affect the entire sport, leading to fears that they would seek to stage the World Cup more regularly and only permit it to be hosted in the most lucrative markets, such as the USA. Fifa said it would “carefully select long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests in FFE. All net benefits of FFE will be reinvested back into football worldwide.”

Infantino is expected to be re-elected unopposed as president next year despite the huge controversy he attracts, but under Fifa statutes must stand down in 2031 after serving three full terms. The Times reported, however, that Infantino has aspirations to serve as chair of the new commercial company, which could earn him tens of millions of dollars.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso plays down Welbeck and Henderson moves after Chelsea win
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso refused to confirm Chelsea are interested in signing the veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson after his first game in charge of the team, a 6-4 pre-season victory against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday, but said he was looking to build a squad that had “proper balance”.

Chelsea are understood to be in talks over a surprise move to sign the 35-year-old Welbeck from Brighton, with the club also reportedly interested in signing the 36-year-old Henderson from Brentford. The links to two Premier League stalwarts reflects a revised transfer strategy under Alonso, with Chelsea seeking to recruit more experienced players into their squad as opposed to focused solely on signing young players, often tying them to lengthy contracts.

“I’m sure that from today to the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of links, a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them, it’s going to be a hard task,” Alonso said. “But for sure, we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance. We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team.”

The new Chelsea manager fielded a youthful side at the Accor Stadium at Sydney Olympic Park in Homebush, with Liam Delap and Tosin Adarabioyo the most experienced members of the starting lineup. Alonso waited until the 63rd minute to bring on a host of star names, including Cole Palmer and João Pedro. The Brazilian forward, who missed out on a place in Carlo Ancelotti’s World Cup squad, made a significant impact off the bench, scoring a hat-trick in just nine minutes as Chelsea took control of the game against their A-League opponents.

João Pedro scored 20 goals during an excellent debut season for Chelsea, having arrived from Brighton for £60m 12 months ago, and asked about the player’s mood before the upcoming campaign, Alonso said: “Very hungry. João is really, really determined to have a great season. He wants to, after a great last year, when he scored many goals. He wants to keep scoring more and more.”

A number of Chelsea’s youngsters showed plenty of promise, with the 17-year-old Dastan Satpayev opening the scoring after six minutes. The Kazakh forward is yet to sign officially for the club and is playing in pre-season as a triallist. His opening goal came from a defence-splitting pass from another teenager, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, with Satpayev smashing the ball home at the near post.

Chelsea’s back four struggled in the first half against a lively Wanderers frontline and their reported new set-piece coach, Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee, will have plenty to work on judging by the ease with which Brandon Borrello and Anthony Pantazopoulos won headers from a corner as the latter scored at the back post for the hosts.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming on as a second-half substitute. Photograph: Mark Evans/EPA

The Wanderers took the lead through Aydan Hammond before a lovely finish from the Portuguese midfielder Dário Essugo made it 2-2 at the break. The goals kept coming in the second half when the left-back Landon Emenalo, who impressed going forward, saw his clearance deflected into the path of Dylan Scicluna, who put the Sydney side 3-2 ahead. Alonso then turned to his bench and his substitutions made an immediate impact. João Pedro held off a number of challenges on the edge of the box before pulling the ball back to Jamie Gittens, who fired home from close range.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But this topsy-turvy game, which felt like England’s third-place playoff against France at the World Cup and finished with the same scoreline, provided more entertainment as the Australian side went ahead for a third time after Estêvão Willian lost possession on the edge of his own area. Awan Lual was on hand to slide the ball through Robert Sánchez’s legs to put his side 4-3 ahead.

The Wanderers, who are also in pre-season, again failed to hold on to a lead as Chelsea overpowered a team that finished bottom of their domestic league last season. João Pedro looked sharp as he showed great composure to score twice in five minutes, before scrambling home an effort from a corner to wrap up his match-winning exploits.

João Pedro’s performance was in stark contrast to that of Delap, who has been repeatedly linked with a move away from west London. The 23-year-old endured another frustrating evening for Chelsea, going close on two occasions but failing to find the back of the net. Assessing Delap’s attitude since returning from the summer break, Alonso said: “I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football, feeling good and he’s doing great.”

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy head coach with Claudio Ranieri named technical director
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini has agreed to be Italy head coach for a second time, the president of the Italian Football ​Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malagò said on Tuesday, also confirming Claudio Ranieri would take over as technical director.

Mancini replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession, and returns to a job he held between 2018 and 2023. He led the national team to European Championship glory in 2021 with a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley but then failed to reach the 2022 World Cup and a slow start to Euro 2024 qualifying. In total, Mancini managed Italy for 58 matches during his first spell and at club level has managed Inter, Fiorentina and Manchester City, where he spent three years and guided them to their first Premier League title in 2011-12.

“Mancini is the coach,” Malago ‌said on Tuesday. “I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

The former FIGC technical director ‌Paolo Maldini and his adviser, Leonardo, resigned from their roles on Monday after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as head coach was blocked because of the former midfielder’s ties to a Russian betting firm. Pep Guardiola was the association’s first choice but turned down the job last month.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini. The 74-year-old, who led Leicester City to the Premier League title in ​2016, will oversee technical operations and ​elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. “I needed someone with ​whom I could share ‌the decision on ​the coach, because ​without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s back’: Zinedine Zidane named France head coach in long-awaited homecoming
Sports.content:
For Tuesday’s front page, L’Équipe simply went with “Il revient” – “He’s back” – echoing the newspaper’s 2005 headline when Zinedine Zidane came out of international retirement. At the time, the midfielder’s upcoming return was seen as a major boost to Les Bleus’ ailing World Cup qualifying campaign. There was a similar sense of anticipation now as the roads around the French Football Federation headquarters in Paris were closed off for Zidane’s unveiling as head coach. A crowd of France fans had gathered outside by the overground Métro tracks with flags, flares and drums, as more than a hundred journalists and TV cameras were ushered into the building.

The fact that Zidane would be next in line to lead France after Didier Deschamps had been an open secret for several years and by the end of the World Cup his arrival was all but confirmed. The new head coach entered the press conference room on Tuesday morning only minutes after his appointment was confirmed by the FFF’s executive committee, but the feeling in France was that the occasion was a couple of decades in the making.

“It’s a new cycle,” the FFF president, Philippe Diallo, said after a preamble in which he paid tribute to Deschamps’ 14-year tenure. Talks with the 1998 World Cup hero, Diallo said, began in February 2025, the month after Deschamps announced he would step down this summer. “Zinedine Zidane is one of the legends of French football and he had made it known that it was one of his dreams to manage the French national team,” Diallo said. “We wanted someone with the aura, the ability, and the hearts of our fans and the French people to manage what is one of the best national teams in the world.”

View image in fullscreen France supporters gather in Paris to celebrate the confirmation of one of the greatest players in Les Bleus’ history as their new head coach. Photograph: Teresa Suárez/EPA

For Zidane, this announcement was the culmination of nearly half a decade of waiting in the wings. “I had several offers from clubs in the last four to five years, but I turned them all down for France,” the former Real Madrid manager said. “The national team is the only thing I wanted. I’ve been with the French teams since I was a kid, all the way up to the senior team. I’m a bit emotional. You might not be able to tell, but I am incredibly excited.”

Zidane declared it was the greatest day of his managerial career. “It’s an immense joy. I am ready for the challenge.”

The five years that have passed since the end of Zidane’s second spell in Madrid will have been spent preparing to take over Les Bleus. “I’ve been watching France as a supporter, but also as a future manager. I don’t think there are any traps. It’s new to me, but I’m not scared. This is what I wanted.” The 54-year-old’s first public appearance as head coach was light on the details of his plans for the national team. He notably sidestepped a question about whether Kylian Mbappé would retain the armband, insisting that he would have to meet the team and its “extraordinary players” first of all. “We need to keep this team winning,” he said, adding that he was impressed with what he had seen during the World Cup.

“I was a No 10 in my playing days,” he said when asked about the style of play he would look to implement. Whether his answer implies a continuation of Deschamps’ attacking shift remains to be seen, but his answers did hint at some kind of change of direction. “Laurent [Blanc] was Laurent, Didier was Didier, and Zizou is Zizou,” he said playfully.

One of Zidane’s long-term objectives will be to compete with the reigning world champions, who have now beaten France in three consecutive tournament semi‑finals. “I spent 25 years in Spain and you know what that means,” he said, before pointing out that the task ahead went beyond beating La Roja. “I know Spanish football very well, but they won’t be the only opponents. You have to beat all of the teams.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was sent off by Horazio Elizondo for butting Italy’s Marco Materazzi in the chest in the 2006 World Cup final. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Zidane’s four-year contract will begin next month, with his extended staff to be unveiled a few weeks before the first internationals of the new season. “We’ll see each other again in September to talk about it. It’s a good thing that we’ll have three weeks with the players.” The focus for now, Zidane said, is on his first match in charge, which will be in Turkey on 25 September.

His homecoming, meanwhile, will be against Italy, just over 20 years after his dramatic exit from the international stage. If the raucous reception as he stepped out of the FFF headquarters is anything to go by, it will be one of the more memorable evenings in the Stade de France’s history.

Sports.title: Wrexham face Liverpool with Premier League still in their sights despite setback
Sports.content:
The Wrexham co-owner Ryan Reynolds called it a “punch-me moment” – his club playing Liverpool in a pre-season friendly at Yankee Stadium just five years after he and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) completed their takeover of a club languishing in the National League. The knockout blow would be playing Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League in 2027-28 and the manager, Phil Parkinson, accepts there is expectation on Wrexham to complete their remarkable rise through the divisions next season.

Parkinson’s team face Liverpool with confidence in the Bronx on Wednesday having defeated Manchester United and Leeds in pre-season so far and moved on from the anguish of missing out on the Championship playoffs on the final day of last season. The near-miss was undoubtedly a setback to an ambitious club’s grand vision but finishing seventh in the Championship at the first time of asking, Parkinson insists, was an accomplishment that should not be dismissed lightly.

The Wrexham manager said: “If we’re honest, to say five years down the line we’d have finished seventh in the Championship we would have said that was going to take some going. To get three promotions back-to-back-to-back is unheralded. Even though there’s always been ambition within the club and we’ve had resources, to take the club from the National League to seventh in the Championship is a lot of big steps and particularly the one last year. League One to the Championship is a huge step.

“Of course we would have loved to have got in the playoffs but I think the staff and the players should be really very proud of their achievements because that was a tough ask, especially with making so many changes.”

Wrexham are among the favourites for promotion next season but are the only Championship club not to make a signing – though a deal for Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray is close – and will not be the only well-funded team with that aim, given the parachute payments available to relegated West Ham, Burnley and Wolves.

“I think the division is going to be stronger this season with the teams coming down,” Parkinson says. “We’ve got work to do within the squad to make us competitive again. We’re close to one signing but we need several more before the window closes. We have to be patient and we will be, but the squad’s not where we want it to be, to be competitive to meet the demands of a Championship season.

“It is going to be a tough second season, we know that, but we feel there is more to come from the existing group. It was difficult last season with a lot of players coming in later and having to relocate to the area and settle as the season started, but they were great for us and I feel there is more to come this season.”

Sports.title: Sunderland close in on Dayann Methalie signing after Newcastle back off
Sports.content:
Sunderland are poised to sign the long-time Newcastle target Dayann Methalie from Toulouse. The France Under-21s defender, who can play left-back or wingback and also operate in the centre, has attracted widespread interest this summer but Régis Le Bris now appears close to acquiring him for about £26m.

Newcastle had extensively scouted Methalie, who made 27 Ligue 1 appearances for Toulouse last season, and reportedly tried to sign him in January. The club have now indicated they opted against the idea of recruiting the 20-year-old and have not submitted a bid this summer. Nonetheless, Methalie appeared an ideal fit for Newcastle’s new transfer policy of recruiting young players in the £20m-£40m price bracket.

Sunderland can offer the 6ft 2in defender Europa League football and he is understood to have verbally agreed a five-year deal at the Stadium of Light, where he would not merely be coached by a compatriot in Le Bris but be part of a sizeable contingent of French-speaking players including Enzo Le Fée, Nordi Mukiele and Habib Diarra. Methalie will be Le Bris’s second summer signing after the arrival of the Belgium right-back Thomas Meunier, who arrived on a free transfer after leaving Lille.

While Methalie is likely to face considerable competition from Reinildo to establish himself as Sunderland’s first-choice left-back, his amalgam of impressive recovery pace, robust physicality and assured left foot have seen him shine as a left-sided central defender in a back three and a back four.

Newcastle, meanwhile, remain in the market for cover at left-back and right-back, with the latter position one Eddie Howe is particularly anxious to reinforce after Kieran Trippier’s departure at the end of last season.

Howe’s hopes of keeping Bruno Guimarães appear to still rest on Arsenal’s willingness or otherwise to pay a fee in the region of £80m for the 28-year-old captain, who has been on a post-World Cup holiday in Brazil and is due to return to Newcastle on Friday, before travelling to a training camp at La Manga with the rest of the first-team squad.

Joe Willock’s future at St James’ Park also remains uncertain. Although Newcastle have rejected an offer in the region of £10m from Besiktas for the former Arsenal midfielder, they appear open to selling him, albeit for a fee closer to £20m.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester United to sign Juve’s Francisco Conceição?
Sports.content:
As sports fans everywhere eagerly await the resumption of cricket’s County Championship season, what better way to while away a few minutes than to contemplate the latest football transfer rumours?

Manchester United and Michael Carrick want to sign the 23-year-old Portugal winger Francisco Conceição from Juventus. The tricky former Porto player, who recently returned from the World Cup, is valued at about £43m (€50m). United are also said to be ahead of Chelsea in the race to snap up Alex Scott from Bournemouth.

Real Madrid, meanwhile, have increased their offer to RB Leipzig for Yan Diomande – whom Leipzig had hoped to replace with Conceição – to about £98m. Reports in Germany say further talks are in order to get the deal for the 19-year-old Côte d’Ivoire international over the line.

Liverpool have emerged as favourites to sign the France international Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, having reportedly held preliminary talks with the 23-year-old over a lucrative transfer.

Bruno Guimarães continues to be the subject of strong interest from the Premier League champions, Arsenal. Newcastle, naturally, have insisted the Brazilian is not for sale, but personal terms have reportedly been agreed between the Gunners and Guimarães’s people, so a bid is surely imminent. Arsenal are also being linked with Vinícius Júnior, with Mikel Arteta apparently determined to sign the Madrid and Brazil forward. Speculation reached fever pitch on Tuesday when it was reported Vinícius would not train this week, further increasing uncertainty over his future. José Mourinho is keen to keep the winger.

Paris Saint-Germain have distanced themselves from a move the for all-conquering Manchester City midfielder Rodri, but the Premier League club expect an offer from Real Madrid.

Seemingly having fought off Chelsea’s pursuit of Granit Xhaka, Sunderland are ready to boost their defensive options by signing the full-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.

Over in Spain, it has been reported that Sevilla are ready to sell Ruben Vargas for about £17m and Aston Villa, Newcastle and Brighton are among potential suitors in His Majesty’s Premier League.

Leeds are poised to confirm a £40m deal for James Trafford, who re-signed for Manchester City after a couple of seasons at Burnley, while Manchester United are keen to send Joshua Zirkzee on a season-long loan to Juventus, with an option for the Bianconeri to buy the 25-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea have held talks with the Brighton forward Danny Welbeck (35) and are also keen to sign Jordan Henderson (36). Welbeck knocked in 13 Premier League goals for the Seagulls last season and was fancied as a possible option for England at the World Cup, while Henderson made the cut, only to suffer a freak wrist injury. Chelsea are presumably drawing up eight-year contracts for both veterans.

In Germany, Borussia Dortmund have agreed to sign the midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas from Racing Genk in Belgium, for a fee that could rise to £32m.

And John Stones, a free agent after leaving Manchester City, has moved closer to completing his move to Inter as reported in these pages: a deal has been verbally agreed.

Sports.title: Milos Kerkez: ‘I’m delighted – Andoni Iraola is the perfect fit for Liverpool’
Sports.content:
It has been quite the summer for Milos Kerkez. There was time at home in Serbia, holidays in Montenegro and Spain, a frantic knock on his bedroom door one day to tell him that Arne Slot had been sacked, an unexpected reunion with Andoni Iraola shortly afterwards, and thousands of well‑wishes sent his way after being photographed escorting a bride into church in his hometown of Vrbas. Congratulations on the wedding are also extended at the start of our interview on a rooftop terrace at Liverpool’s team hotel.

“No! This is wrong, everyone gets this wrong!” the full-back exclaims. “It was my oldest brother. In Serbia it is normal for the younger brothers to take the bride to the church. That’s what I did and now everyone thinks I got married. It was Rade, not me. There are three of us – Rade is the oldest, I’m the youngest and Marko is the middle one. I keep having to explain to people that I never got married. I was going around the club when we started back and people were congratulating me. I’m like: ‘No, I’m not ready for this yet!’”

Well, that’s one way of breaking the ice with an interviewee. Marriage is categorically not on the agenda for Kerkez, a humorous and engaging force of energy, but he is ready to embrace other responsibilities: notably stepping out of Andy Robertson’s shadow and stepping up at Liverpool. Early days, of course, but it has been noted during Liverpool’s pre‑season training camp at Chicago Fire’s performance centre how the 22-year-old and his fellow Hungary international Dominik Szoboszlai have taken a leading role among a relatively young squad.

Kerkez – who was eligible to play for Hungary through his paternal grandparents – is in an advantageous position as the Iraola era begins with gruelling double training sessions and a pre-season friendly win over Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. He knows the new boss better than any other Liverpool player, having matured into a £40m left-back during two seasons with Iraola at Bournemouth. He knows he doesn’t have to win over the new head coach as Iraola rates him highly. And he knows that, to convince Liverpool fans after a difficult debut season at Anfield, he is now working for a coach who can bring the best out of him.

View image in fullscreen Milos Kerkez tussles with Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga during a difficult debut season at Anfield. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

“I was delighted, honestly,” Kerkez says on discovering Liverpool’s choice to replace Slot. “He helped me and improved me a lot in the two years I spent with him. I was really happy, obviously for myself but also for the team. Everyone knows what type of football he plays so I think he is the perfect fit for us.

“It’s the intensity. He’s not scared to play one-on-one all over the pitch, to press high and to be on the front foot always. If you see footage of how we all are after training, all lying down, then you can see what he is preparing us for. You definitely need legs and good condition for what he wants us to do, but we will be all right. When we play games with three or four teams he calls it ‘consequences’ and the losing team and the team that finishes second has to run. How much you have to run depends on what he decides in that moment, but there is always running for the team that loses.

“He’s intense and he likes details. He’s very professional. He likes to talk sometimes but not a lot. I think maybe he doesn’t want to get too close to some players and wants to show that everyone is the same in the team, so he doesn’t want to get too close to anyone in particular. He keeps it professional, with a lot of hard work.”

There were times last season when Kerkez appeared inhibited by Slot’s insistence on building from the back and full-backs coming inside. It was his pace and energy up and down the flank with Bournemouth that had attracted Liverpool and earned him a place in the Professional Footballers’ Association’s team of the year in 2024-25. He should be able to play to his strengths more often next season.

As he explains: “The gaffer likes to play more with the full-backs down the line, underlapping, overlapping. It worked well for me at Bournemouth, so I think it will also work well for me here. He always told me that defending is really important, for him that is first of all, and because you are a full-back you need to defend really hard. Everything you can do in front of you is like a bonus. So I was always focused first on defending and then running forward to help the wingers. He showed me that when you do your job then you are free to do what you want, so I felt really free with him. He lets you be more free to do your stuff.”

Not that Kerkez blames Slot for last season’s turbulence, far from it. The pair remain in contact. “I was surprised,” he says of the Dutchman’s sacking, 12 months after delivering the Premier League title. “I really didn’t know. I was back in Serbia, I was sleeping and my brother woke me up. He knocks on my door and it was a big surprise. Nobody knew. I couldn’t believe it, I was like: ‘Wow.’ I have been in touch with him since, we have exchanged a few messages.”

View image in fullscreen Milos Kerkez celebrates scoring at a time he was playing brilliantly well for Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Kerkez admits last season was “tough for everyone” at Liverpool as every time the team seemed to have solved one problem, another would appear. As part of the expensive recruitment drive of last summer that failed to bear fruit – though Kerkez achieved far more than others – the scrutiny on the left-back and his fellow new signings was particularly intense. He insists he did not feel it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Honestly, I don’t care about pressure,” says the full-back, who will face Wrexham in the second game of Liverpool’s US tour in New York on Wednesday. “I don’t like ‘pressure’ and that stuff. I grew up a bit different in Serbia. We grew up different. You could say maybe we are built a bit different. For example, I started to drive a truck when I was 10 years old.” Sorry? “It was with my dad,” Kerkez says. “I climbed in and then I took the wheel. He was doing the pedals, I was only quite small so I couldn’t reach them.”

Kerkez’s father, Sebastijan, still drives his son to Liverpool’s training centre on occasions. He and Kerkez’s mother, Tijana, moved to England to help their second son settle into life as a Premier League player. “They are very important,” says the defender. “My brothers have their own lives now but my parents are with me and I am much happier they are with me. My dad is here to smack me sometimes on the top of the head and to remind me. Sometimes you play a few good games and maybe you start to get a bit carried away. But my dad is here to smack me. I come straight back down and I switch straight back on.”

Another important influence on Kerkez has been Robertson, the man – and the Liverpool legend – he was bought to replace. The Scotland captain and now Tottenham left-back regularly took Kerkez aside last season to pass on his experience. But there was no big parting message when the time came for Robertson to say goodbye to Anfield in May.

“I didn’t want to get a lot on to him,” says Kerkez, who became close friends with Mohamed Salah last season. “He was a bit emotional as everything was coming to an end. I didn’t want to get on to him too much, but throughout the year he helped me. We had a few conversations about crosses and about the big lungs we need to have so we can run until tomorrow. He did a lot of seasons, I should also have the same. We had conversations like that. Also, where to put the last ball, to focus, to put your head up and sometimes put better crosses in.

“We all know what Andy did for the club. I’m not running away from that. I want to make my own way. I’m going to work hard. I know what it means to play for Liverpool. I showed it a bit last year and I am going to show it more this year. Before we left the Axa [Liverpool’s training ground, to come to Chicago] I saw on TV a show about how many goals and assists Mo had, it was something like 380. I just walked out! ‘What is this?’ I was thinking. Time flies. A new generation comes and hopefully everything will be good.”

Sports.title: UEFA lay into FIFA over 'proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup' in a move that could 'make president Gianni Infantino millions' - as plan is labelled a 'nuclear bomb' for football
Sports.content:
UEFA have hit out at a leaked FIFA plan to sell stakes in the World Cup in a move that could make its president Gianni Infantino millions.

News broke in The Times on Tuesday afternoon that FIFA boss Infantino was considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could be worth around £15billion.

The report added that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, a highly lucrative position that estimates suggest could pay him more than $50million-a-year.

The bank JPMorgan is said to be handling the process and the Donald Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

The proposal has already received widespread criticism from across football, with one source telling The Times it would be a 'nuclear bomb' for the sport and another arguing it would 'potentially be much worse than the European Super League'.

It is understood the English FA were completely unaware of the proposal.

And UEFA, which has been critical of FIFA and Infantino's actions in recent times, hit out at the plans.

FIFA are reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup in a hugely contentious move

UEFA launched a strongly worded statement slamming plans that 'crossed a line' (pictured - UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin)

'This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,' they said in a statement. 'UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association.

'So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.'

If the move was to go ahead, the global football calendar would likely be affected.

For example, the Men's and Women's World Cup may be expanded or held more regularly than every four years, while the Club World Cup could face similar changes.

As part of the proposal, all 211 member associations would have stakes that would make up 20 per cent of the total company and be worth around $20million (£15million) each.

That is a larger figure than many of their annual revenues, and they would be given the option to sell them to raise funds.

FIFA would retain a majority stake in the new entity and private investors would be able to take on minority stakes.

Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, was reported to be one of the potential investors

FIFA are a not-for-profit organisation and enjoy tax-free status at their HQ in Switzerland.

For the most recent cycle of 2022-2026, their revenue is expected to be around $15billion (£11.3billion) – much of which came from this summer's World Cup – meaning this would provide a lucrative opportunity for individuals to be involved in.

The Times added that the blueprint for the potential selling of stakes has been discussed among senior FIFA figures and potential investors, which could include Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared – and they have signed non-disclosure agreements.

Some of those potential investors are understood to have even spoken internally about 'buying FIFA'.

Infantino's proposed new role could be extremely lucrative. Figures close to the plan are said to see it on a par with the NFL, whose commissioner Roger Goodell earns about $64million a year.

The reports come at a time when Infantino is already under fire for a variety of reasons following the World Cup.

This includes the US visa restrictions that affected supporters and officials from many countries, the extremely high prices of tickets and Infantino's links with Trump, which came to a head after Folarin Balogun's red card was suspended following a phone call by the US President to the Swiss administrator.

When contacted for comment, FIFA confirmed plans to launch a new body called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which they described as a 'controlled subsidiary consolidating FIFA's commercial and event operations'.

They added that 'FIFA would retain sole control of FFE and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions,' and claimed the move would increase the funding available to all 211 member associations.

The Daily Mail Sport also contacted the White House for comment.

Sports.title: Newcastle insist Arsenal have NOT made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap... and Ajax want return for West Ham's Edson Alvarez: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Newcastle insist Arsenal have NOT made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap... and Ajax want return for West Ham's Edson Alvarez: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Black Cats zero in on Methalie

Sunderland are continuing talks over a potential £26million deal for left-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, the France Under 21 international defender, who can also operate as a centre-back, emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle United.

But Regis Le Bris is hopeful Sunderland can bring him in on a five-year contract for what would be a record sale for Toulouse.

Dayann Methalie (right) emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle

Forest putting out feelers for Famalicao's Sa

Nottingham Forest are in talks to sign Portuguese attacking midfielder Gustavo Sa from Famalicao.

The 21-year-old was a target for Saudi Arabian clubs earlier in the year and West Ham this summer but Forest may now sign him and then send on loan to Olympiacos.

Sa was the captain of Famalicao last season, scoring four goals and claiming two assists from 34 appearances.

Tomiyasu training with Palace

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is training with Crystal Palace after the expiry of his contract at Ajax.

The Japan international was expected to extend his contract but is a free agent after making just nine appearances since moving to Amsterdam on a short-term deal in January owing in part to a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old is training with Palace in Como as part of the club’s pre-season preparations and could feature in a friendly this week. He has had interest from Venezia and Sassuolu, too.

Palace are playing in the Como Cup. They face Lens, new manager Pierre Sage's former side, tonight then take on Famalicao in two 45-minute games.

Takehiro Tomiyasu

Bees eye Sarr signing

Brentford are weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

The Bees were looking to strengthen their options even before news of Jordan Henderson's proposed departure for Chelsea.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabate from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future. They now want two more for the first team squad with Henderson heading towards Stamford Bridge.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Pape Matar Sarr is on Brentford's radar, with Jordan Henderson wanted by Chelsea

Newcastle still waiting on Arsenal bid for Bruno

Newcastle United insist they have still to receive a formal approach from Arsenal for midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing to make an official £70m-plus move for the Brazilian who is keen to join them but, so far, Newcastle sources say any proposals have come via the player's agent.

Newcastle manager Eddie Howe said at the weekend he was unsure what would happen over the 28-year-old's future.

Bruno Guimaraes wants to move to Arsenal but Newcastle say they are still waiting for a bid

Delap in demand with Chelsea set to sign Welbeck

Nottingham Forest remain among the list of clubs showing interest in Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Danny Welbeck's pending arrival from Brighton is likely to leave fewer opportunities for 22-year-old Delap and clubs are enquiring to ascertain the deal required to sign the former Ipswich Town forward.

Forest, Everton and Newcastle United are just some of the clubs who have expressed interest in the former England U21 international.

Meanwhile, Forest have made an offer for Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili as talks for Feyenoord's Givairo Read also continue.

Both players are also appreciated by Bournemouth and Newcastle United.

Liam Delap is a target for several clubs with his chances at Chelsea likely to be limited

Jorgensen leaves camp for France

Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen has left their camp in Australia ahead of joining sister club Strasbourg.

The 24-year-old Denmark international made 12 appearances for Chelsea last season and wants regular first team football.

On my Edson! Ajax want West Ham's Alvarez back

Ajax are trying to re-sign West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Dutch side sold Alvarez to West Ham for £35million in 2023 and now hope to buy him back.

West Ham want around £12.5m but Ajax sources say they are still owed money from the way payment was structured on the original transfer.

The 28-year-old, who has spoken to Ajax director Jordi Cruyff, spent last season on loan at Fenerbahce and was part of Mexico's World Cup squad but has generally struggled to live up to expectations since leaving Amsterdam.

Real Sociedad are also interested in Alvarez but are proposing a smaller, structured deal.

Edson Alvarez in action for Mexico against England at the World Cup

Rock on Tommi to Meadow Lane

Aston Villa winger Tommi O'Reilly is in talks to join League One Notts County on loan.

The 22-year-old had been set to sign for Sheffield Wednesday but, after further discussions, Villa have decided Meadow Lane may suit his development better.

O'Reilly had an outstanding campaign with Crewe last season and Villa hope he can replicate that form under Notts County coach Martin Paterson.

Notts County also signed Australian forward Luka Smyth from Finnish top-flight side VPS yesterday for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.

Notts County are in talks over a deal for Villa's Tommi O'Reilly

Perri set for Italian job after Trafford deal

Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri is expected to join Torino on loan with an option to buy once a deal for James Trafford is completed.

Trafford, 23, is poised to sign a deal worth around £130,000 a week once Manchester City and Leeds finalise details on an expected £40m transfer with £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Torino and Leeds have agreed an initial loan move for Perri for the coming season. The deal also includes an option to buy him permanently next summer.

Leeds goalkeepers Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier have left Daniel Farke’s squad to join Manchester United and Arsenal this summer.

They would still like another as cover as well as strengthening at left-back, attacking midfield and striker.

Lucas Perri's Torino deal may be signed off after James Trafford arrives from Manchester City

FRIDAY: Real open talks for Yan Diomande, Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back

Sports.title: Cricket must throw the book at the club at the centre of 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal - there is no place for such disgraceful antics in the 'gentleman's game', writes ALEX BYWATER
Sports.content:
Cricket is commonly known as the ‘gentleman’s game’ with those who take part traditionally placing a significant emphasis on fair play, etiquette and mutual respect.

Such values seemingly haven’t landed at Saltburn CC after the North Yorkshire club was embroiled in a cheating storm that has gone viral online and on social media.

The video evidence appears damning. Multiple clips show slip fielder Brian Devine clicking his fingers as the ball passes the batsman to mimic the sound of an edge.

Devine’s aim is as clear as it is shocking – to con the umpire into giving his team a wicket. It’s hard to always agree with Piers Morgan, but the television personality nailed it when being just one of millions to have his say on the incident. Morgan, who is a big cricket fan, described Saltburn’s antics as ‘outrageous cheating’, a ‘shameful scam’ and ‘pathetic’.

Spot on.

The North Yorkshire and South Durham League has launched an investigation into Saltburn, Devine and its players.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

The cheating storm involving the Saltburn player has gone viral on social media with Piers Morgan labelling it as ‘outrageous cheating’, a ‘shameful scam’ and ‘pathetic’

Norton batsman Noman Shabir protested that he didn't touch the ball after being given out

An investigation has been launched by the North Yorkshire and South Durham League, who must throw the book at Saltburn and Devine to send a message there is no space in cricket for these antics

It must throw the book at them and in the process send a message that there is no place in cricket – no matter the level at which it is played – for such disgraceful antics.

The same applies to any other sport.

Cheats must always be punished. And just like Australian cricketers Cameron Bancroft, Steve Smith and David Warner were in 2018 for their roles in the sandpaper ball-tampering, the same must apply to those at Saltburn.

Long bans and points deductions should be the bare minimum for those found to have been part of the subterfuge once the investigation is complete. It’s vitally important that a message is sent to those who play grassroots cricket that any sort of attempt to fool an umpire is unacceptable.

The officials at that level have a hard enough job as it is. As someone who plays grassroots cricket in south-east Wales, I know that all too well. I’ve been on the wrong end of my fair share of disputable leg before wicket dismissals.

Only last weekend, I saw my team-mate given out caught behind when the ball quite clearly came off his thigh pad. These incidents can be hugely frustrating, but there is an acceptance (after a few lagers) that they are human error.

What has happened in the case of the umpires who have taken charge of Saltburn matches is that they have been hoodwinked.

Pure and simple. I have played club cricket for a long time and never seen anything like it.

One question must be asked of Saltburn and Devine.

Just how desperate do you have to be to try and win a game of recreational cricket by resorting to such means?

Their actions have painted what is supposed to be the ‘gentleman’s game’ in an awful light.
