An amateur village cricket team is at the centre of a cheating scandal that has gone viral across the world after one of their fielders was accused of tricking umpires by clicking his fingers to imitate the noise of an edge off the bat.

An investigation has been launched by the North Yorkshire and South Durham League into the cheating allegations against Saltburn Cricket Club after video footage emerged online.

In the footage shared widely online, Saltburn's first slip appears to fool the umpires by clicking his fingers to get the batsman out.

Now the Daily Mail can reveal the cricketer at the centre of the storm is 'legendary' amateur player Brian Devine.

Mr Devine, 38, has played for years at Saltburn Cricket Club and is well known on the cricket scene in North Yorkshire.

A prolific batsman, he also previously played for Pudsey St Lawrence Cricket Club, helping them to win the Bradford Premier League second tier championship in 2023.

Following this achievement, he returned to Saltburn for the start of the 2024 season, with one social media post noting: 'Excellent batting on Saturday from returning legend Brian Devine. 95 runs.'

There was such excitement about his return that he even managed to secure a sponsorship deal with local Indian restaurant Spices of Saltburn.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his actions on the cricket field

Saltburn player has been caught on camera clicking his fingers whenever ball was near bat

Norton batsman Noman Shabir protested that he didn't touch the ball after being given out

Mr Devoine, a father-of-one, from Guisborough, Cleveland, works as a company secretary at Northallerton Auctions, which specialises in auctions for livestock and farm machinery.

When contacted about the viral video by the Daily Mail, and told he had been identified as 'Clicky Ponting', Brian responded 'Naturally I can't comment on that.'

Then when told he was being widely accused of cheating, and asked whether there was some other explanation for what takes place in the videos, he said: 'I don't want to talk about it. I'm at work.'

From his social media posts, in addition to his obvious love for cricket, Brian also appears to be a big fan of Boris Johnson.

In one post from 2022 he wrote: 'Top man Boris. Others may try to put you down! I won't have a bad word said! I am off to get my kettle.'

The accused cricketer's mother-in-law today told the Mail he is a 'man of integrity.'

Georgina Vaughan, the mother of Devine's partner Clare, said the family had been shocked by the scale of the cheating row.

She said: 'It was only a little village cricket match and now it's become this thing that's all over the news and social media.

'It has got totally out of hand and there is nothing that any of us want to say.'

Asked whether Devine was a man of integrity, she replied: 'He certainly is.'

Footage from Saltburn's 2nd XI match with Norton Cricket Club in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League last weekend showed a ball delivered by Saltburn bowler Sam Morrison passing the bat of Norton batsman Noman Shabir without making contact with it.

At the same time, Mr Devine playing at first slip seems to click his fingers.

When Saltburn wicketkeeper Josh Bowes takes the ball, Saltburn appeal and the umpire gives Shabir out.

Shabir can clearly be seen objecting to his dismissal and seems to indicate to the umpire that he did not hit the ball and that the noise heard was a clicking of fingers instead.

The clip and other similar evidence have attracted international media attention and gone viral online and on social media.

A statement from the North Yorkshire and South Durham League read: 'The League has received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday 25th July 2026. A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete, no further comment will be made.'

Saltburn won their match with Norton by a mammoth 159 runs.

Devine has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' - in a light-hearted reference to Australia legend Ricky Ponting.

That's as far as the funny side goes though with the likes of Piers Morgan condemning the actions.

Taking to X, the avid cricket fan wrote: 'Outrageous cheating, and just the tip of the iceberg from all that's come out since it was exposed.

'Clicky Ponting (as he is now known) and various teammates at Saltburn CC, have clearly been at this shameful scam for years. Imagine doing this in local amateur cricket? Pathetic.'

Other clips online appear to show Devine clicking his fingers to cheat umpires and earn dismissals unfairly in other matches.

One such example is a video showing footage of a match between Saltburn and Middlesbrough second XI.

Outrageous cheating, and just the tip of the iceberg from all that’s come out since it was exposed. Clicky Ponting (as he is now known) and various teammates at Saltburn CC, have clearly been at this shameful scam for years. Imagine doing this in local amateur cricket? Pathetic. https://t.co/fFOusuys4u — Piers Morgan (@piersmorgan) July 28, 2026

Other incidences have been found of Devine clicking his finger in previous matches for wickets

The North Yorkshire and South Durham League have begin a full investigation into Saltburn

Saltburn have been widely-condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

The actions of Saltburn have been described as 'the worst case of cheating' seen in cricket online, with it likely that long bans will be handed out. Unconfirmed reports online suggested that Devine has already been suspended for the rest of the season by Saltburn. Daily Mail Sport approached both Saltburn and Norton for comment but did not receive a reply.

In 13 matches across 2026 with Devine as the slip catcher, Saltburn's wicket-keeper has taken 39 catches. In seven matches without Devine, the wicket-keeper has taken just five.

In addition to the numerous video clips seemingly showing Devine clicking his fingers online, further suspicion over Saltburn's antics has been aroused by the scorecards of previous matches.

On July 18, Saltburn's second XI played Shildon Railway CC with wicketkeeper Bowes taking a mammoth eight catches. Such a number is highly unusual. The record number of dismissals for a wicketkeeper in a Test match innings is seven. Bowes is averaging almost four catches per match in eight games this season. The investigation remains ongoing.

It is the responsibility of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League to investigate any allegations of cheating or complaints over the behaviour of teams as well as imposing any sanctions. As such, it is unlikely that at this stage the England & Wales Cricket Board – as English cricket's governing body – will get involved directly.

Sports.title: Ascot Gold Cup winner Scandinavia continues march to flat racing greatness in Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup
Sports.content:
Ascot Gold Cup winner Scandinavia continues march to flat racing greatness in Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ryan Moore declared Scandinavia an 'unbelievable stayer' after the Ascot Gold Cup winner continued his inexorable march towards flat racing greatness with a decisive victory in a dramatic Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup.

The Aidan O'Brien-trained son of Justify, game winner of the Group 1 prize 12 months ago, was expected to face stiff competition defending his crown with Ascot runner-up Trawlerman again in opposition.

However, a re-enactment of the Royal meeting's titanic tussle failed to materialise as Scandinavia powered eight and a half lengths clear of the front-running Trawlerman, himself intermittently hampered by the riderless Amiloc who lost rider Hector Crouch exiting the stalls.

The Goodwood stewards deemed that Amiloc was a runner and, while Moore felt his ongoing presence had little impact on the race, Trawlerman's rider William Buick felt the incident affected him valuable momentum.

'It definitely had an effect and it's unfortunate. The winner won well but when you get hampered at that stage of the race it's never ideal,' he said.

Referring to the loose horse who crossed the line in front of Scandinavia, Moore quipped: 'He was just a bit disappointed he didn't get by him!'

Ryan Moore has declared Scandinavia Scandinavia an 'unbelievable stayer' after success in the Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup

'Scandinavia is an unbelievable stayer. I couldn't say he is better than Kyprios as he had a nearly perfect race record once he went over a staying trip but so has this lad now.

'When we ran in the Gold Cup it was his (Scandinavia's) first time over two and a half miles and, having been beaten by Trawlerman in the past, I didn't want to eyeball him too early.

'I ended up doing that after all at Ascot, but he had enough class to overcome it.'

HKJC World Pool Lennox Stakes winner Lake Forest could be set for a busy week as he is also an intended runner in today's Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes.

The well-backed 10/11 favourite collared pacesetter and defending champion Witness Stand inside the final furlong and had enough in reserve under Cieren Fallon to see off a late thrust from Rogue Diplomat to land the Group 2 by a neck.

Maureen Haggas, wife and assistant to trainer William, said: 'The owners are up for it (running again), and we have plenty of time to decide.

'He has got nothing until York and does not have to do any travelling. He is pretty laid back, so unless something happens overnight, I would imagine that is the plan. If he is okay, why not?'

Sports.title: County cricket transfers: Sussex finally land first signing under ECB sanctions, England star signs new Durham deal, the issue holding up James Vince's Hampshire contract and Gloucestershire snap up Indian spinner
Sports.content:
Sussex have signed Joey Evison on a multi-year deal from 2027 in a landmark move ratified by the ECB.

Under the spending restrictions the ECB placed upon Sussex for recording an operating loss of £1.33million last year, county cricket’s managing director Rob Andrew must approve new player signings at Hove until the end of the 2028 season.

Evison is the first arrival of this period, having found chances to play in his favoured role increasingly limited at Kent, partly due to the emergence of another ex-England Under 19s all-rounder in Ekansh Singh. In his two most recent County Championship appearances for the club, Evison was carded at No 8, the same position he occupied in the one-day loss to Gloucestershire on Sunday.

The 24-year-old is leaving Kent with a year remaining on his contract after a deal was struck that is financially favourable to both clubs.

Viewing batting as the stronger of his two suits, he went on loan to Leicestershire last month, striking 55 in the innings win over Yorkshire and claiming combined figures of three for 87 across two appearances.

Evison was touted as one of the country’s brightest prospects when Kent signed him from Nottinghamshire four years ago and some supporters will be disappointed that a player with 14 half centuries in 45 first-class appearances at an average of 31.65 is departing the club early.

Sussex have signed Kent all-rounder Joey Evison, who had to go on loan to Leicestershire this month after being unable to get into the team

The 24-year-old won man of the match in the 2022 One-Day Cup final as Kent beat Lancashire at Trent Bridge

He also has 68 wickets at 43 and two Metro Bank Cup hundreds on his CV, winning man of the match in the 2022 final when Kent beat Lancashire at Trent Bridge.

The move reunites him with his former Kent coach Matt Walker, who is taking over from Paul Farbrace at Sussex next season. With all-rounders Fynn Hudson-Prentice, who is joining Hampshire, and Danny Lamb among those leaving the club in the next few weeks, opportunities should be plentiful.

Sussex are also in talks to add Middlesex seamer Blake Cullen to a group that will be without Tom Alsop in 2027 after a deal was struck with Gloucestershire. Daily Mail Sport first flagged the potential move for the left-hander in April, when it was announced Ben Charlesworth would be swapping Bristol for Lancashire next year.

Alsop, 30, had 12 months remaining on his deal with Sussex and will continue to live in Hove, but is moving early on a three-year deal having been limited to two Division One outings this summer due to the form of Tom Clark at No 3.

Sussex have already lost rising fast bowling star Henry Crocombe to Surrey, a signing that concluded a scramble among Test-hosting counties. Yorkshire and Nottinghamshire also went in strongly for the 24-year-old, who was called into England’s second Test squad against New Zealand last month as cover for county team-mate Ollie Robinson.

A knock-on of that business was James Taylor agreeing to leave Surrey for Yorkshire, scuppering Worcestershire’s plan to pair him with his brother Tom in a new-look new-ball attack next season. Somerset, Gloucestershire and Glamorgan were also interested.

Potts stays put

Daily Mail Sport understands Matthew Potts has committed his future to Durham beyond September following enquiries from Yorkshire.

The Sunderland-born England seamer, 27, is looking to regain his place in the national team after a tricky Ashes last winter Down Under.

Daily Mail Sport understands Matthew Potts has committed his future to Durham beyond September following enquiries from Yorkshire

Patterson-White is Notts for sale

Another north-easterner in Liam Patterson-White is also staying put with Nottinghamshire, signing a three-year contract after listening to an offer from Warwickshire, who failed to replace the experienced Danny Briggs when he returned to Sussex last winter.

Slow left-armer Patterson-White is comfortably the most prolific spin bowler across the Championship’s two divisions this summer, with 32 wickets at under 24 runs each.

Midlands battle for keeper Cox

Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire are understood to be contesting the capture of 34-year-old wicketkeeper Ben Cox, who is leaving Leicestershire in September.

Only the Hampshire-bound Rishi Patel has scored more top-flight runs for the Foxes than the 530 contributed by Cox in 2026.

Shaikh up at Leicestershire

Leicestershire have made an investment for the future by snapping up Warwickshire’s ex-England Under 19s captain Hamza Shaikh on a three-year contract from 2027, while spinner Liam Trevaskis’ future at Grace Road remains uncertain.

Hampshire eye new deals for key batsmen

One soon-to-be free agent whose negotiating position has improved significantly in recent weeks, though, is Hampshire batsman Joe Weatherley, the most prolific run-scorer in this year’s T20 Blast.

While Ali Orr is expected to leave the Utilita Bowl for Middlesex, Weatherley enjoys working with coach Russell Domingo and is understood to be keen to stay, particularly if his preference to bat lower down the order in four-day cricket is met.

Hampshire’s T20 captain James Vince is finalising a new deal with the club that is complicated not by financial demands, but the limited number of days he is permitted to work in the UK now that he is a resident of the United Arab Emirates for tax purposes.

Hampshire batsman Joe Weatherley enjoys working with coach Russell Domingo and is understood to be keen to stay

Indian duo snapped up

With the Championship returning in three weeks, counties have turned their attention for recruitment for the season finale, with Yorkshire securing India’s left-arm wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav for three September fixtures following a five-match Metro Bank Cup stint, and Gloucestershire welcoming his compatriot Ravi Sai Kishore - who bagged 11 wickets in two matches for Surrey last year - for the final six rounds.

Gloucestershire are rooted to the foot of the Division Two table, 43 points behind second-bottom Lancashire, but director of cricket Jon Lewis says the arrival of Sai Kishore is an indication of their desire to avoid the wooden spoon.

Who'll Toole up for 2027?

One other potential signing for this period of the campaign is Ray Toole, the left-armer who was the leading wicket-taker in New Zealand’s Plunket Shield last winter.

Toole, 28, previously played for Essex and Durham and is known to be of interest to several counties for 2027. However, with the crammed county schedule affording just two-day gaps between first-class matches, he could yet be snapped up on a shorter-term deal covering this August and September.

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane is announced as France's new manager on a four-year-deal - as football icon succeeds former team-mate Didier Deschamps
Sports.content:
Zinedine Zidane has been announced as France's new manager, with the long-expected announcement having finally been delivered.

The 54-year-old has signed a four-year deal with Les Bleus as he succeeds his former Juventus and France team-mate Didier Deschamps.

Deschamps left his 14-year tenure as France manager at the end of the World Cup, with his side losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain in the semi-finals. They finished fourth after a 6-4 defeat by England in the third-place play-off.

Zidane's unveiling took place on Tuesday morning at the French Football Federation's (FFF) headquarters in Paris, alongside FFF president Philippe Diallo.

It is Zidane's first foray back into management since leaving Real Madrid in 2021, revealing he has rejected offers in the meantime as he waited for his 'dream' to become France boss.

'The French team was the only thing I wanted to do,' Zidane told reporters.

Zinedine Zidane has been announced as France's new manager on a four-year contract

He revealed he has rejected club management roles as he waited for his 'dream' job instead

Zidane succeeds Didier Deschamps (centre) who bowed out at the end of the World Cup

'I've always looked at this team through the eyes of a future manager. I didn't take a club job for that reason. The only thing I wanted to do after Madrid was manage the French national team.

'I could have taken on a three-year role because Deschamps was there. He made that decision in January 2025, and the very next day I knew I wanted to be the next one. We met with the president and the deal was sealed.'

Deschamps oversaw 185 matches and 120 victories, guiding France to the 2018 World Cup title, the 2020-21 Nations League trophy, and the Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup finals.

He and Zidane share a long association, having been team-mates in France's 1998 World Cup-winning side on home soil.

Zidane played a pivotal role in that triumph and won the Ballon d'Or that year. He made 108 appearances for the national side, scoring 31 goals and contributing 29 assists.

'You'll see my [team's] style soon,' Zidane said. 'I'm driven by the game. I was a No 10, and what drives me is scoring goals.

'I lived in Spain for 25 years, you know what that means. On the pitch, I was a leader. Now I'm becoming a leader through my experience.

'Winning in '98 is the best thing that's ever happened to me, winning with my team-mates. I spent those four or five years waiting for that day. I'm emotional; you can't see it, but I'm so excited. I'm happy.'

The pair were team-mates at Juventus and France as players (pictured for Les Bleus in 2000)

Speaking about Zidane's arrival, Diallo revealed that negotiations with the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000 winner began in February 2025 after Deschamps said he would stand down after the 2026 World Cup.

'This is an exceptional moment, exceptional because of the person sat next to me,' Diallo said. 'Zinedine is one of the legends of French soccer and for many years he said one of his dreams was to take charge of the France team.'

'I would like to thank Didier Deschamps and his staff for their work. For 14 years he led the France team to the top.'

The length of the deal means Zidane will work through until at least the 2030 World Cup, incorporating two Nations Leagues (2026-27 and 2028-29) as well as Euro 2028 before the major showpiece.

His first match in the hotseat will be away to Türkiye in the Nations League on September 25. After that comes a trip to local rivals Belgium on September 28 with a clash against Italy on October 2 sparking his first game in charge on home soil.

Sports.title: Nine-minute hat-trick hero Joao Pedro is 'very hungry' after Brazil World Cup snub, says Xabi Alonso - as Chelsea boss opens up on Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson pursuits
Sports.content:
Nine-minute hat-trick hero Joao Pedro is 'very hungry' after Brazil World Cup snub, says Xabi Alonso - as Chelsea boss opens up on Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson pursuits

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Xabi Alonso described Joao Pedro as ‘very hungry’ after Chelsea’s striker scored a nine-minute hat-trick in Sydney, having been left at home by Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti for the World Cup.

The 24-year-old was surprisingly ignored by Ancelotti this summer, and in a friendly win over Western Sydney Wanderers, he replaced Liam Delap while his side were trailing 3-2.

Joao Pedro assisted Jamie Gittens for the equaliser before scoring three times himself for a 6-4 victory.

‘He is very hungry,’ Alonso said when asked about Joao Pedro being snubbed by Brazil. ‘Joao is really, really determined to have a great season. He wants to keep scoring more and more.

'We need to help him. On his own it's not possible. He will have the players around him. It’s not just about the striker, but every time we win and our striker scores, I am happy.’

On Delap, who could leave this summer to make way for Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old at Brighton who Daily Mail Sport revealed is a transfer target, Alonso added: ‘I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football, feeling good, and he's doing well.’

Joao Pedro scored a hat-trick as Chelsea beat Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 in pre-season

Blues boss Xabi Alonso said the striker is 'very hungry' after missing the World Cup with Brazil

Asked about wanting to add experience, with Chelsea looking at Welbeck and Brentford midfielder Jordan Henderson, 36, Alonso said: ‘Everyone has to learn. Everyone. It doesn't matter if you are young, if you are more experienced, this is what happens in the game.

‘This is a quality as well that you need. You can be quick. You can be good at dribbling. But you can have this game intelligence to do the things and from everything we need to be quick because the competition is in just almost a month and we want to get ready for that.

‘We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team. For that we have an idea, we have a plan, and let's see how we set it up until the start of the Premier League.’

Asked specifically about Welbeck, Alonso said: ‘No comment.’

Romeo Lavia received no minutes in this friendly because of a minor hamstring issue. In his place, 16-year-old Reggie Watson was the only player to complete a full 90 for Chelsea, and the son of former Crystal Palace and Wigan footballer Ben impressed in the centre.

As did Dastan Satpayev, the 17-year-old who arrived this summer from Kazakhstan side FC Kairat. ‘He is really strong, really quick, and you will be really impressed with him,’ Alonso said.

Sports.title: Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton
Sports.content:
Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton

An investigation has now been launched into Saltburn’s 2nd XI cricket match with Norton in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League

View 2 Images A village cricket game is being investigated

Village cricket has been rocked by a cheating scandal after a fielder was accused of clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of the ball hitting the bat.

‌



Footage appears to show a slip fielder for Saltburn 2nd XI snapping his fingers just before his wicketkeeper takes a catch. The batter appears confused to be given out.

‌



After the clip circulated, people accused him of fooling the umpire into thinking the batter had edged the ball.

‌



Ben Mummery, who shared the footage on social media, said: "Click-gate has gone viral and I’m genuinely really happy it’s being exposed. Harshest possible punishment please. It’s not cricket."

England cricket icon says wife was left 'suicidal' over Azeem Rafiq racism storm READ MORE :

View 2 Images An investigation has been launched into Saltburn’s match with Norton after cheating allegations (Image: Saltburn CC)

‌



The incident happened in a match in the North Yorkshire and South Durham League (NYSDL) between Saltburn 2nd XI and Norton 2nd XI, while ­Saltburn were fielding.

League leaders Saltburn ended up winning by a huge margin of 159 runs at their home ground in North Yorkshire.

Rory Cotterill, who captained Middlesbrough CC’s 2nd XI in a 29-run defeat to Saltburn in June, has since claimed a similar situation occurred in that match. He shared a video online which allegedly showed the same player clicking his fingers.

Article continues below

The NYSDL confirmed it received a formal complaint regarding S­aturday’s game.

It said: “A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made.”

Saltburn CC has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

Unmissable in-depth analysis of all eight races on the second day of the Festival which stages the week's signature race, the Sussex Stakes

View 6 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap: CANNES is entitled to a plea of mitigation following his Royal Ascot blowout and deserves another chance.

‌



A debut second to his stablemate James J Braddock at the Curragh last November, the son of Sea The Stars took the silver medal home from his return to action at Leopardstown in April, but went one better in handsome style at the Foxrock venue the following month.

‌



Joseph O’Brien then gave Cannes his handicap debut in the King George V Stakes punters bought into the plan - my selection went off the 7-2 market leader in a field of 19.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

His supporters were left out of pocket when Dylan Browne McMonagle’s mount returned in 14th place behind his Ryan Moore-partnered stablemate Enceladus - but there are excuses.

Despite the big field, the leaders didn’t go off at a breakneck pace and the race unfolded to favour those positioned nearer the front than the back, which is where Cannes found himself during the early stages.

The handicapper has left Cannes on an unchanged mark of 95 and that’s a rating that looks within range for a colt who has plenty more to offer, while the unstoppable form of his trainer’s team is another reason to be cheerful.

‌



Of the remainder, Hatteen , Infraad and, at bigger odds, Parisian Scholar are three-year-olds open to further progress who have a role to play.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 CANNES, 2 HATTEEN, 3 PARISIAN SCHOLAR

View 6 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

‌



2.25 British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes: WILD BLOSSOM is a two-year-old filly of significant promise who should make full use of this drop in class.

The daughter of Mehmas - dam Duchess Rose didn’t win but is a half-sister to Queen Elizabeth II Stakes hero Bayside Boy - cost 300,000 guineas at the breeze-up sales in April before being sent to join Karl Burke by owners Wathnan Racing.

Making her racecourse debut in a four-runner novice stakes for fillies over five furlongs at Carlisle the following month, Wild Blossom could hardly have been more impressive, sent to the front by James Doyle inside the two-furlong pole before careering away to humble Crownbreaker by 10 lengths.

‌



Sent off at 7-1 for the Group 2 Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot, my selection completed in 10th, beaten just over four lengths, behind winner Victorious, with four of today’s opponents in behind.

But that effort merits an upgrade as subsequent events at the meeting showed the far side, where Wild Blossom finished third in a group of 11, was at a disadvantage to the stands’ rail. With her sights lowered to conditions-stakes level, Wild Blossom is expected to get back to winning ways before returning to Group company.

Fast Track, 14th in the Queen Mary before a runaway success at Beverley, is a strong candidate for the podium, along with Weatherbys Super Sprint winner Zigazig Ah and Hidden Gift.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 WILD BLOSSOM, 2 FAST TRACK, 3 HIDDEN GIFT

View 6 Images Simon Crisford: trains Newsboy's pick with son Ed

5.00 Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes - ZANTHOS hasn’t yet reproduced the form of her two-year-old season - but there’s no time like the present.

‌



Roll the clock back to the autumn of 2025 and the daughter of Sioux Nation, trained in tandem by Simon and Ed Crisford, was proving herself in a higher grade than the company she’s keeping today.

A debut winner at Newmarket in August, Zanthos was unexpectedly beaten at odds of 4-11 at Leicester a month later. But she left that form well behind when outpointing The Prettiest Star by half a length for the Group 2 Rockfel Stakes back at Newmarket on her final start as a juvenile. It’s no calumny against Zanthos to say things haven’t worked out so far this term.

Returning in Longchamp’s Poule d’Essai des Pouliches in May, Oisín Murphy’s partner finished ninth of 15 behind Diamond Necklace and, stepping back from a mile to six furlongs, she came back 16th of 22 in the Group 1 Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot won by Venetian Sun.

‌



But seven furlongs on fast ground are the conditions that have shown Zanthos, fitted with a tongue strap, in her best light and the drop to Group 3 level will help her bid to bounce back. Flora Of Bermuda carries a penalty for her success in York’s Group 3 Summer Stakes 19 days ago but is feared most, ahead of Planet Seeker and Radiant Beauty.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ZANTHOS, 2 FLORA OF BERMUDA, 3 PLANET SEEKER

View 6 Images Kaiya Fraser: won on Adonius at Chester (Image: PA)

‌



3.35 Veuve Clicquot Molecomb Stakes: ADONIUS is the choice to give Co Durham trainer Rebecca Menzies a winner at Goodwood with her first-ever runner at the track.

The son of Soldier’s Call is already the best horse dual-purpose trainer Menzies has handled on the Flat - and is still a long way from the bottom of the barrel.

Reputed to be full of spirit during his pre-training days, Adonius was gelded prior to his debut at Musselburgh at the beginning of April but channelled his energies in the right direction to score by seven lengths.

‌



Adonius had just a neck to spare over Rlasthope under a penalty in East Lothian eight days later but did enough to earn a trip to Chester’s May fixture, where he contested the curtain-raising Lily Agnes EBF Conditions Stakes.

Again in front from flagfall under Kaiya Fraser, my selection took his record to 3-3 with a length-and-a-quarter dismissal of Hickory Lad.

Menzies resisted the temptation to go to Royal Ascot with Adonius, whose train-to-catch way of doing things will be well suited to the South Downs as he moves up to Group 3 level, and her patience can yield its reward.

‌



Pershaada, Ruler’s Pride and El Floridita were all beaten in different races at the royal meeting but warrant respect, all the same.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ADONIUS, 2 PERSHAADA, 3 EL FLORIDITA

View 6 Images Bow Echo (right) wins by a short head from Gstaad (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

‌



4.10 Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes: BOW ECHO has yet to taste defeat and is expected to take the score in his private battle with Gstaad to 3-0.

A perfect 3-3 as a two-year-old - he won a Newbury maiden, Haydock Park’s Listed Ascendant Stakes and the Group 2 Royal Lodge Stakes at Newmarket - the Night Of Thunder colt went into his winter quarters as one of the leading candidates for the 2,000 Guineas.

Bow Echo was an uneasy 9-2 chance on the big day, despite one upbeat bulletin after another from trainer George Boughey in the lead-up to the Rowley Mile test on the first Saturday in May.

‌



In the event, Billy Loughnane’s partner defied the market drift, coming from the back of the field to lead at the furlong pole and holding Gstaad by two and three-quarter lengths at the line, the pair a whopping eight lengths clear of third home Distant Storm.

Bow Echo went off at 5-6 to confirm that superiority over his Aidan O’Brien-trained rival in the St James’s Palace Stakes and did so - but only by a short head.

The result suggests that the momentum is with Gstaad, but Bow Echo tended to over-race after being leant on by the runner-up leaving the stalls yet demonstrated another facet to his game in being able to win ugly.

‌



It’s not hard to share Boughey’s view that Goodwood’s contours will play to Bow Echo’s strengths and he receives the vote to remain unbeaten.

Sports.title: Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’
Sports.content:
Loose horse causes Goodwood Cup chaos after getting in way in ‘important part of race’

Trawlerman was practically stopped in his tracks by the riderless Amiloc in the straight before Scandinavia completed an impressive victory in the Group 1

View 2 Images Scandinavia chases the loose Amiloc at Goodwood (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

A loose horse caused chaos in the £500,000 Goodwood Cup after getting in the way ‘in the most important part of the race’ on Tuesday.

‌



The 2m Group 1 was supposed to produce a rematch between Ascot Gold Cup first and second, Scandinavia and Trawlerman, the horse who trains in special goggles to protect his eyes from the sun.

‌



Yet there was drama from the outset as first Trawlerman anticipated the start to burst out of the gate half a length in front of the rest. Then Amiloc lost his rider Hector Crouch who, after a valiant effort to stay in the saddle, was dumped on the turf.

‌



The riderless Amiloc decided to race ahead of the field, with Trawlerman kept a safe distance back leading the rest of the field.

But as soon as William Buick launched his bid for victory, Amiloc came right across the front of him, forcing the jockey to take evasive action to avoid a collision. With momentum lost, Scandinavia forged clear to win by eight and a half lengths.

Describing the interference afterwards, Buick said: “It’s significant. It’s hard to say how significant. He got in the way in the most important part of the race. It definitely had an effect.”

‌



View 2 Images Hector Crouch goes off the side of Amiloc (circled) as Trawlerman (far side) steals an advantage (Image: ITV)

Trainer John Gosden said: “When you’ve been crossed like that and checked, he’s not the type to turn around and start quickening. We got the worst of it and we went from being a length and a half in front to a length and a half behind. That’s racing.”

The stewards report said: “Approximately 2 furlongs out, the riderless AMILOC edged right-handed towards the rail resulting in the rider of TRAWLERMAN (IRE) having to take a check for a number of strides when placed on the heels of AMILOC, but after viewing a recording of the incident, it was found that no riding offence was involved.”

‌



After looking into the incidents at the start the stewards were satisfied that Amiloc was a runner “as the rider was mounted as the start was effected before AMILOC jumped left-handed, resulting in Crouch catching his leg on the starting stalls, causing him to become unbalanced and ultimately unseated shortly after the start.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The report added: “TRAWLERMAN (IRE), drawn 8, anticipated the start and accelerated the gate at the same moment as the start had been effected, thereby enabling the gelding to break quickly. Being satisfied that it was not caused through a faulty action of the starting stalls, no further action was taken.”

Article continues below

Scandinavia’s jockey Ryan Moore said: “He couldn’t have done anymore than what he done today. I never asked him for everything.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory

Anthony Joshua was dropped twice in the opening round by Kristian Prenga on Saturday night, but rallied to a stunning second round knockout in Saudi Arabia

View Image Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

A member of Anthony Joshua's team has brutally hit back at Simon Jordan after the talkSPORT presenter questioned the Brit's knockout victory over Kristian Prenga.

‌



'AJ' returned to the ring on Saturday night for the first time since being involved in a tragic car crash over in Nigeria which resulted in the deaths of close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion was dropped twice in the opening round by the Albanian, but sensationally rallied to a second round knockout victory. Joshua's remarkable win has guaranteed a date with long-time rival Tyson Fury - which is due to take place before the end of the year.

‌



Yet Jordan was rather sceptical of the end result, writing: “Not having that … #anthonyjoshua fight. Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how’s that ? … Prenga totally different in 2nd. Something not quite right , all designed to rinse maximum amount of money …”

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Jake Paul and Eddie Hearn team up in shock move to end heated rivalry READ MORE :

Sergey Lapin, Director of Team Usyk, has since brutally hit back at Jordan's remarks. Joshua teamed up with the Ukrainian's team prior to his bout with YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul back in December - and Lapin once again played a key role on Saturday night.

In an interview with Action Network, Lapin said: "What do I think of Simon Jordan’s comments? I suppose they also told Prenga to walk straight into a punch that weighed one and a half tonnes. Everyone is entitled to their own theories. I have a friend who still believes the Earth is flat and that space doesn’t exist. Personally, I’d rather discuss what actually happened inside the ring than someone else’s imagination."

Kristian Prenga's team addresses conspiracy theories after Anthony Joshua loss READ MORE :

Lapin was quick to turn his attentions to Joshua versus Fury, and is confident his man can secure a devastating knockout over the 'Gypsy King.' "Time certainly plays a role. It helps you recover, refine your game, and sharpen your timing. But time alone doesn’t win great fights," he said.

Article continues below

"When it comes to Joshua versus Fury, I genuinely believe AJ can knock Tyson Fury out. This is the kind of fight where one mistake changes everything. Both men have what I call a “red button”—one decisive shot capable of ending the night. The question isn’t whether the fight happens in one month or six. The question is who finds that moment first. That’s why I believe AJ can finish the fight inside the distance."

Sports.title: Jack Grealish left OUT of Man City pre-season squad as reason for absence confirmed
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish left OUT of Man City pre-season squad as reason for absence confirmed

Manchester City star Jack Grealish saw his loan spell at Everton cruelly cut short and the winger has now been denied the chance to join the club on their pre-season tour of Asia

View 2 Images Jack Grealish will not join Man City on their pre-season tour of Asia (Image: Getty Images)

Jack Grealish has been left out of Manchester City’s tour of Asia as he continues his recovery from long-term injury. The former £100m man returned to the Etihad Stadium this summer following a loan spell at Premier League rivals Everton.

‌



Grealish spent the entire 2025/26 campaign with the Toffees, but saw his contributions limited after picking up a foot injury.

‌



And while Grealish will be desperate for a chance to impress new boss Enzo Maresca, he will not be getting that for the time being. Grealish’s foot injury has been cited as a key reason for his omission from the City squad.

‌



City are set to take on Inter Milan in Hong Kong before clashes with the K-League All-Stars and Atletico Madrid in South Korea. Grealish, 30, has just one year remaining on his contract with his current employers.

John Stones decides next club after England star holds talks with Chelsea READ MORE :

Erling Haaland told he is NOT one of Premier League's 10 best ever strikers READ MORE :

"At the moment, he's here. He's a Man City player," new City boss Maresca said of Grealish last week. "I always said the same. In any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club.

"It's my duty to try to coach them. Jack is here. I have a good relation with Jack since I left. Also, we keep in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and he's a very good guy. So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens."

‌



Grealish has made 157 appearances for City in all since his mega-money switch from boyhood club Aston Villa. In that time, he has scored just 17 goals but contributed to three Premier League titles and a Champions League success.

View 2 Images Grealish has not played since sustaining a foot injury while with Everton (Image: Getty Images)

Grealish has already been tipped for a move abroad should he leave City this summer by ex-Villa star Gabby Agbonlahor. He said: “It will be interesting to see what happens with Jack, if he's given a chance by Maresca.

‌



"He would have been part of that Man City squad that Maresca was at (as assistant). Or, will the manager think, 'No', and will Jack think, 'Do you know what? Maybe I want to move on'.

"I think it's still early doors, I think we have to see what happens over the next six weeks, there's still six weeks left of the transfer window… I don't see him staying there, I see him moving on.

"It wouldn't surprise me if he moves somewhere else in Europe, I don't see him staying in the Premier League. I think he's still got one year left on his contract, the wages as well, will that be a problem for some clubs maybe in the Premier League? But don't rule out maybe going back to Everton, David Moyes loved him."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino plots to SELL World Cup after Donald Trump talks in ‘nuclear bomb’ for football
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino plots to SELL World Cup after Donald Trump talks in ‘nuclear bomb’ for football

Plans for selling stakes in FIFA to private investors have emerged under a highly controversial scheme, with UEFA condemning the proposals

View 2 Images Plans have emerged which could see stakes in the World Cup and FIFA reportedly made available to private investors. (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. The organisation has confirmed that they will invite third parties to make a 'minority, non-controlling investments' into the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

‌



Bank J.P. Morgan have engaged to work alongside FIFA while other advisers such as OpenEconomics are engaging with prospective long-term investors. Infantino and the FIFA administration will control the development of the project while outside investors will have a minority stake with no operational role.

‌



The administration of US President Donald Trump has reportedly been consulted about the plan, which would see a company being formed to control FIFA's men's and women's competitions, the World Cup and Club World Cup. Each of the 211 member associations would receive a stake which they could retain or sell for income.

‌



Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

The Times has reported that one senior figure within football regards the plan as a "nuclear bomb" for the game, as the proposals suggest that FIFA would own the majority of the company, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations receiving a small stake totalling 20 per cent.

UEFA have released a statement condemning the report. They said: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously.

"So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

‌



"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The venture is said to have raised concerns that private investors could put pressure on the men's World Cup being staged in countries where commercial success can be maximised. The report adds that American businessman Joshua Kushner, whose older brother Jared Kushner is married to Trump's daughter Ivanka, is seen as the main investor along with bank JP Morgan.

‌



The 56-year-old Infantino is set to be re-elected as the FIFA president until 2031 with no competitor for his position. The move to a new model could see Infantino become commissioner, with some suggesting the salary for that position could be on par with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell who earns $64million (£48m) a year, around 10 times as much as the FIFA chief's earnings.

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino alongside US President Donald Trump. (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Infantino has come in for criticism following this summer's World Cup across North America. The ticket prices, logistics surrounding the tournament and Trump's interference, which saw USA international Folarin Balogun's ban suspended, sparked intense scrutiny.

‌



A week after the tournament, the 56-year-old launched a tirade accusing critics of spreading hate. He posted a 15-slide, 887-word statement on Instagram, saying: "My message for all those who…

"To everyone who missed our beautiful game, the emotions, the celebrations, the laughter, the crying, the deception, and the joy. To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness.

"Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
